conformanceSummary.story-048: All checked criteria hold. _dispatch, _psmDonate and every kept setter/auth/rescue function are byte-identical to BalancerPoolerV2 once the contract-name prefix is normalised. The Balancer surface and imports are removed. The constructor checks {token0,token1}=={sUSDS,phUSD} in either order, records the sUSDS index and reads no reserves. pool() carries onlyAuthorizedPooler/whenNotPaused/nonReentrant, reverts on zero floors (custom error) and on an empty pair, computes the closed-form s from in-tx reserves (formula matches the plan exactly), swaps then adds with LP to=address(this), checks liquidity>=minLP, resets approvals, and emits Pooled(sUSDSIn,s,phusdOut,liquidity). There is no price ceiling and no pauser(). quotePool mirrors the router's optimal-amount selection and the pair mint maths. Extra guards (NothingToPool, InsufficientSUSDS, AmountTooSmall) are additive and sit on the concrete contract.
conformanceSummary.story-049: All checked criteria hold. BALANCER_VAULT, BALANCER_POOL, unlockCallback, the IUnlockCallback inheritance and the balancer imports are removed, and a case-insensitive grep for balancer|unlock returns nothing. _swapSusdsForPhusd uses the existing UNIV2_ROUTER swapExactTokensForTokens along [sUSDS, phUSD] (phUSD constant = 0xf3B5...D605) with to=this, an exact approve and a reset to zero. pool() now reverts on minPhusdOut==0. Legs B and C, _dispatch and the setters are unchanged (comment-only diff).

findings.specText: story-048: "Kept verbatim. `_dispatch`, `_psmDonate` ... Keep all events, errors and storage semantics the dispatch suite relies on."
findings.actualBehavior: Because the code was copied verbatim, the documentation defect logged as F-01-047 on BalancerPoolerV2 was copied too. The DonationSkipped NatSpec says it fires on 'PSM outage / fee spike / dust', and the _dispatch NatSpec lists 'dust' among the failures that 'park the USDS'. In _psmDonate (line 353) a dust sweep (gemAmt == 0) is a clean no-op, so no revert reaches the catch and DonationSkipped is never emitted. UniPoolerV2's new contract-level NatSpec (lines 29-32) leaves dust off its list, so the contract now contradicts itself.
findings.deviation: This is a documented-behaviour deviation inherited from F-01-047, not a code defect. It matters for retention: BalancerPoolerV2 is deleted in story 050, at which point F-01-047 would close as code-removed while the same wrong documentation lives on in the replacement.
findings.relatedLedger: F-01-047 5d6538f76f (open, BalancerPoolerV2). This is a new instance on a different contract, not a reopen.
findings.recommendation: Drop 'dust' from the DonationSkipped and _dispatch NatSpec in UniPoolerV2. This is a comment-only change and does not breach the verbatim-code clause.

findings.specText: Plan Stage 2 step 7: "Register with the Pauser." Step 10: "Retire the old pooler: pause it and unregister it from the Pauser." Plan Stage 1a test: "Dispatch still works while the pooler is paused." Versus story-048 Concerns: "Do NOT add a `pauser()` ... `Pauser.register` requires `IPausable(c).pauser() == Pauser`, dispatchers have none" and "The plan's test 'Dispatch still works while the pooler is paused' contradicts the code."
findings.specSource: phStaging2 docs/BalancerWinddownPlan.md §4 Stage 1a / Stage 2 vs story-048 doc Concerns + Autonomous Decision 5
findings.actualBehavior: The code follows the story, and the story is authoritative: UniPoolerV2 has no pauser() and cannot be registered with the Pauser. pause() is onlyMinter (base), and pausing blocks dispatch, which means index-4 mints, as well as pool(). Read literally, plan steps 7 and 10 are unexecutable: register would revert and BalancerPoolerV2 was never registered. The plan's safety intent of stopping pooling without stopping mints is still achievable, through owner incrementAuthVersion(), which mass-revokes pool() and leaves _dispatch untouched. Neither document names that lever.
findings.deviation: The plan and the story conflict, so the spec is ambiguous. There is no code deviation. The risk sits downstream: the phStaging2:100/103 cutover script and its preview/verify keys are written from the plan.
findings.recommendation: Amend the plan: delete Stage 2 step 7's Pauser registration and step 10's unregister, rewrite the Stage 1a test as 'dispatch works while pool() is unavailable', and record incrementAuthVersion() as the pool-only kill switch. Check this when script-auditor runs on unipooler-cutover.

findings.specText: story-048: "The `_dispatch` override copied **verbatim**" ... "so the NFT minter, the mint-debt hook and NFT index 4 all see an identical dispatcher"; Checklist: "keep `_dispatch` and `_psmDonate` verbatim"; Implementation Notes: "any new guard or modifier belongs on UniPoolerV2, never on `ATokenDispatcherV2`."
findings.specSource: story-048 doc (Story Overview, Technical Details, Checklist, Implementation Notes)
findings.actualBehavior: _dispatch is verbatim and has no hookTypeId or non-default-hook guard. If the cutover omits UniPoolerV2.setHook(hook), the constructor-deployed DefaultDispatchHook stays wired and index-4 mints accrue zero phUSD mint-debt without any error (CODE-001).
findings.deviation: None; the code is faithful. Law-1 evaluation: (1) The story's verbatim clause does forbid the guard where CODE-001 and the M-04 NudgeRatchet fix put it, inside _dispatch. It does not forbid a guard elsewhere on the concrete contract. `hook` is public base storage, so a UniPoolerV2 constructor could take the hook and assign it, which closes the omission window without touching _dispatch. (2) If the story's intent were implemented faithfully, the result would not be exploitable. The harm needs a non-malicious owner to omit a step, it fails open as misallocated mint-debt, and no third party can trigger or profit from it. That makes it a Law-3 footgun, not an unsafe story. So it is not escalated as story-unsafe, and severity stays with CODE-001 (potential-low). (3) If the owner takes CODE-001's in-_dispatch guard, Law 1 outranks Law 2, so the change must not be graded as a story-048 Law-2 deviation in a later run.
findings.relatedLedger: Q-08 96c60b723f (wont-fix 2026-06-17, BalancerPoolerV2 only; its rationale is 'live, will not be retrofitted', which does not apply to the undeployed UniPoolerV2), M-04 c91bef813d (fixed, NudgeRatchet).
findings.recommendation: Fold this into CODE-001 as the story-side annotation. If the owner fixes it, a concrete-only guard (constructor-supplied hook, or a stored defaultHook compared in _dispatch) is Law-1-sanctioned. Record a waiver on story-048's verbatim clause so later Law-2 scans do not flag the guard.

evaluatedNotEscalated.verdict: Not story-unsafe. It is an owner-omission footgun, not an exploit. See FAITH-003.

evaluatedNotEscalated.candidate: 'Deliberately no price ceiling' combined with the plan §5 depth premise (ECON-002)
evaluatedNotEscalated.verdict: Not story-unsafe. The arbitrage skim is a deliberate, bounded design cost (Law 3): each arbitrageur mints at $1 against new collateral. The plan's depth numbers (~33.8k/34.8k) are a factual premise error; seeding with 62.9% of the BPT gives a pool about 1.59x shallower, so $1 arrives at about a $636 zap rather than about $1k. That belongs in ECON-002 (informational, visible), so no separate F entry is filed, to avoid a duplicate. Spec-conformance should cross-reference ECON-002 as a plan-premise error.

evaluatedNotEscalated.candidate: Leg A buys phUSD on the protocol-owned phUSD/sUSDS pair UniPoolerV2 zaps into (CODE-002)
evaluatedNotEscalated.verdict: Not story-unsafe. The venue is the explicit story intent. Most of the swap cost returns to protocol-owned LP, and the cross-call quote interference is an operational keeper-sequencing concern already carried by CODE-002.

evaluatedNotEscalated.candidate: Front-run in the favourable direction succeeds rather than reverting (Autonomous Decision 7)
evaluatedNotEscalated.verdict: Faithful. The checklist's 'reverts on minPhusdOut or minLP' is a protective intent aimed at the adverse (buy-phUSD) shift. A phUSD-dump front-run costs the attacker money on the back-run.

evaluatedNotEscalated.candidate: pair_ is only token-checked, not checked against factory.getPair (relates to CODE-003)
evaluatedNotEscalated.verdict: No criterion is breached; the story asks only for the token-set check. Passing a non-factory pair would desync the reserves pool() reads from those the router swaps against. That is an obvious misconfiguration under Law 3, so it is suppressed here and left to CODE-003's cutover framing.
